key_gap: Both sides produced the identical decision rule — fake-door first (2 wks, ~$2K, ≥120/800 waitlist signups or ≥20% CTR), concierge second (3 wks, ~$12K, ≥40% weekly-active execs), the $450K/12-month build gated on both gates, and the not-tested set (retention/lock-in/expansion) declared — with the same core insight: a 71% stated-intent survey is a prior, not a signal, and only behavior validates. The gap is ordering and ownership: the human downgraded the non-behavioral evidence and named the fake-door as the smallest probe in one first-pass move, priced the option ('kill-now costs $2K vs $450K against a 71% opinion'), and owned the line 'asking is not measuring — only action validates'; the AI reached the identical structure by generating and verifying a full alternative set inside its HOW stage before the smallest test was obvious, stating the insight later and more cautiously, and only then emitting the pre-committed thresholds in its packet.
learning_signal: For assumption-gated commitments, the behavior-first rule is the entire method and should be the first move: (1) restate the core assumption as a behavioral, falsifiable claim (WILL-USE weekly, not 'wants access') and rank existing evidence — stated preference < secondhand claims < behavior — downgrading surveys and anecdotes explicitly as priors, not signals; (2) design the smallest probe that produces ACTION, not opinion, on exactly that claim (fake-door/waitlist before concierge), with cost and duration an order of magnitude below the commitment; (3) pre-commit kill/continue thresholds BEFORE data collection, with the kill path (reallocate the budget) stated; (4) declare what the probe does NOT test (retention, lock-in, expansion) and specify the second learning loop that is earned only after the gates pass — a probe validates one assumption, never the product; (5) price the experiment as an option: kill-now cost vs committing the full spend against an opinion base rate.
suggested_improvement: Add a 'behavior-first evidence gate' to the WHAT/WHY boundary for product/feature decisions: (a) in WHAT, require the core assumption to be restated as a falsifiable behavioral claim and the existing evidence to be classified as stated-preference vs behavior; (b) in WHY, rank evidence sources with stated preference explicitly downgraded before modeling; (c) in HOW, prefer the smallest action-producing probe as the default candidate rather than generating the full alternative set first — add a 'smallest probe' pre-pass; (d) require pre-committed kill/continue thresholds and a 'what this experiment does not test + next loop' line in every decision packet for assumption-gated commitments.

key_gap: The pure style executed its core move correctly and then failed on it: it formed a hypothesis (will clinicians act on Sable's alerts), ran the smallest experiment (2-ICU pilot, ≥40% bar), got a clean behavioral result (80%), declared 'validated, commit' — and that is where the MVP theater began. The pilot measured the LOWEST-risk component (clinical adoption) and was treated as the gate for the entire $2.1M commitment; the gating facts — EMR integration certification (6-9 mo queue), security review (3 mo), HIPAA sign-off (2 mo), production false-alarm rate — were never testable by any small experiment, and when the lead-time facts surfaced the style's reflex was ANOTHER experiment (a sandbox integration pilot before the $525K deposit) that cannot produce certification or sign-offs, would blow the 5-week board gate, and slips go-live ~10 months. The AI performed the testability partition instead: what an experiment CAN touch (adoption — already answered) vs what is commitment-required (certification, security, HIPAA, sunk on every path), committed the deposit and reviews now, ran adoption instrumentation in parallel during the build, and reframed the staged production rollout (with a pre-committed false-alarm-rate stop gate) as the real experiment — the commitment itself is the smallest responsible unit when no experiment can validate the gating facts.
learning_signal: MVP theater — running an experiment that produces a signal on a non-gating assumption while the decision that was required all along slips its window — is the failure mode, not rigor. The core skill is the testability partition: (1) before blessing ANY experiment, partition the assumptions into (a) falsifiable-by-experiment within the decision window and (b) commitment-required (lead times, certification, audit sign-offs, sunk costs); (2) check which partition holds the dominant risk — if (b) dominates, the decision is commitment, and any experiment is scoped to (a) components and run IN PARALLEL with the build, not as a gate before it; (3) verify that a proposed experiment could actually produce the fact it claims to test (a sandbox cannot produce certification; a side-channel pilot cannot produce production false-alarm rates) — if its output cannot change the decision, it is a stall dressed as rigor; (4) price the stall: add the window-slip cost (board cycle, slot queue, exposure-hours) of each 'one more experiment' to the options table like any alternative; (5) when the gating facts are commitments, the smallest responsible unit is the commitment itself, and the production rollout — staged cutover with a pre-committed monitoring gate — IS the experiment.
suggested_improvement: Add a 'testability partition + stall-cost' gate to the WHY stage for commitment decisions: (a) after modeling, explicitly classify each assumption as experiment-testable-in-window vs commitment-required, and emit which gating facts no experiment can produce — treat 'unproducible fact' as a commitment signal, not an evidence gap; (b) run a falsifiability check on every proposed probe: could its output change the go/no-go within the decision horizon? if not, exclude it; (c) add an 'experiment-stall cost' line (window slip, queue loss, exposure-hours) to the alternatives table so delayed decisions are priced like any other option; (d) include a 'rollout-as-experiment' default: when pre-commitment validation is impossible, the selected plan must specify staged cutover with pre-committed stop gates as its learning loop, and parallel instrumentation for any component that IS testable.
